assertions.why: diff-first; the ordering word IS the rule — never post unreviewed
principle 4 — the ordering word IS the rule
structural: debts are collected before the posting step
principle 1 — a docs/handovers/ directory would be a prose ledger

assertions.anchor: names a debt without a filed issue is a principle-4 violation
assertions.why: without the full clause, a rewrite can keep a stray 'never posts one' while deleting the rule that an unfiled debt blocks the close — the exact erosion principle 4 exists to stop
principle 4's sibling question, asked in its exact wording
the skill's hard prohibitions must remain a named section

assertions.anchor: never post a closing comment naming an unfiled debt
assertions.why: drop this and the closing record can name work nobody can find later; the debt lives in prose instead of the issue tracker, which is principle 1 and principle 4 failing together

assertions.anchor: never write the handover to a file in the repo
assertions.why: drop this and docs/handovers/ reappears — a prose ledger competing with the issue tracker for the truth about what closed
drop this and cross-project transfer stops happening silently: nothing else in the convention forces the question, so proven work dies in the repo that proved it

assertions.anchor: never require tokenomics or plumb-line for any function
assertions.why: drop this and the skill becomes unusable in any repo without the sibling plugins installed — the convention stops being adoptable a piece at a time

assertions.anchor: never close the issue itself unless asked
assertions.why: drop this and the skill starts closing units on the builder's behalf; the close is a judgement call about whether the work is done, not a side effect of writing the record
degradation must stay loud by name, not silent

assertions.anchor: do not pretend it was posted
assertions.why: drop this and a missing gh auth yields a record the builder believes is on the issue but that exists only in a terminal scrollback — a silently lost close
drop this and a repo with no dialect note either halts the close or invents labels; the named fallback is what keeps the skill working on an unstamped repo
drop this and an already-closed issue makes the skill abandon the record entirely — the one case where the handover is most likely to be lost is the one it would skip
